question.text: The moment of inertia of a semicircular ring about an axis, passing through the center and perpendicular to the plane of ring, is<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo> </mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mfrac><mo> </mo><msup><mi>MR</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> is the radius and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> is the mass of the semicircular ring. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi></math>.

solution.text:
The moment of inertia of a semicircular ring about a line perpendicular to the plane of the ring and passing through its centre is given as I=MR2, where m and R are the mass and radius of the ring. Comparing the given value

.I= MR2=1xMR2

⇒x=1
